findings.title: Per-client resources suppress all-clients grants
findings.body: When a client-specific resource exists, permission evaluation uses only that resource and never evaluates the `Clients` type resource. A client-specific resource is created as soon as any permission references that client, so an all-clients grant (for example `manage` or `view`) then stops applying to that client. This makes authorization depend on whether an unrelated per-client permission was created and can deny intended grants across the realm; evaluate both the specific resource and the all-clients resource, or otherwise combine their grants.
